theTwoFailures.shortStatement: On the first-offence marijuana possession route the packet omits the component four committed records mark required, and two of that component's three specified sections reach the participant nowhere.
theTwoFailures.whatIsAbsent: nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-legal-effect-explanation-3, role legal_effect_explanation, 'What sealing does, and what it does not do'. The delivered set ships nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-filing-instructions-3 instead.
theTwoFailures.whatTheParticipantLoses: The specified section 'What it does not reach' — 'The order is directed at the court record. It does not by itself change records held by other agencies, and it is not a pardon. If you need a criminal-history record corrected as well, that is a separate request to the agency that holds it.' Grepping this route's six delivered pages returns 'other agencies' 0, 'not a pardon' 0, 'criminal history' 0, 'separate request' 0. The section 'This is not the general sealing chapter' survives only as a clause; its content that 12-60.1's waiting periods, clear-and-convincing burden and 45-day hearing rule do not apply here is absent from this route's pages.
theTwoFailures.whyThePlainReadingIsTheWrongOne: The same artifact tells the participant three times, on the three Chapter 12-60.1 routes, that sealing does not reach BCI criminal history record information. On the marijuana route it says only that this seal is irreversible and 'stronger than Chapter 12-60.1 sealing'. A reader comparing the two is invited to conclude the stronger seal reaches at least as far.

positiveFindingsARepairLaneMustNotUndo.why: The brief asked this lane to record a correct refusal either way, so a repair lane does not undo it. Four correct DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001-A3 refusals were found, one of them the Mississippi refusal the brief named.

findings.theRefusal: The compiled profile src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/MS-mississippi.json holds a $150 filing fee in packetGenerator.feeRules, keyed in its own words to 'each petition to expunge an offense under 99-19-71' via Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72. This family's routes are §§ 99-15-123(3) and 9-23-23. The packet reads the figure and refuses it by name: 'The $150 filing fee you may have read about is levied by Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 99-19-72 on petitions to expunge an offense under Sec. 99-19-71. NEITHER SECTION IN THIS PACKET IS SEC. 99-19-71.' It then names the clerk of the administering court as the authority for both fee and waiver.
findings.confirmedHere: Yes. The profile's fee lines were read in this lane and every one is keyed to 99-19-71; neither 99-15-123 nor 9-23-23 carries a fee statement anywhere in the profile.

findings.theRefusal: The compiled profile src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/CT-connecticut.json says 'Connecticut erasure is free' and '$0 No fee charged (§ 54-142a)'. The string '54-142d' does not appear in that profile at all. This family's route is a § 54-142d petition for physical DESTRUCTION, a different section and a different remedy. The packet quotes the committed registry's own non-establishment verbatim — 'Unresolved. Sec. 54-142a(k) bars a fee on petitions under that section; Sec. 54-142d is a different section and whether the bar reaches it has not been established.' — and names the clerk's office with the registry's venue string attached.
findings.confirmedHere: Yes, by reading the profile in this lane.
findings.doNotRepairThisBy: publishing '$0, Connecticut erasure is free' for a § 54-142d filing. That is the sign-flipped California trap A3 was written for.

findings.theRefusal: The compiled Illinois profile carries a fee table — '~$120-$160 per Request', 'Circuit clerk filing fee ~$60', 'Fee waiver $0 Application for Waiver of Court Fees' — and the route census names that profile as a requiredSourceId for this route, so under A2 it is in scope. Under A3 it does not answer this route: every line is scoped in the profile's own words to the Request to Expunge and/or Seal form set, whose form 4 is the Fee Waiver Application 'for petitioners who cannot afford the filing and State Police fees'. This route is a verified petition to a chief judge, and the profile separately records the Wilma rule that a mistaken-identity fact pattern routes AWAY from ordinary expungement or sealing. The same reasoning carries the service question: the profile's clerk-service and 60-day objection rules are recorded under 'Step 4 - Service and objections' of the Request process.
findings.confirmedHere: Yes, by reading both the profile and the committed route contract src/lib/legal-authority/routes/route-splits.json#IL:criminal-identity-theft-mistaken-identity-relief in this lane. The route contract records no fee, no service and no destination term.
findings.doNotRepairThisBy: importing $120-$160, or importing the Request's clerk-service rule.

findings.theRefusal: The strongest of the four. The packet names the figure the participant will have seen elsewhere and tells them whose route it belongs to: 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28... It belongs only to the no-petition route under Government Code Sec. 411.072(c)... This is a petition route under Sec. 411.0731. Do not arrive at the clerk's window with $28.' It then states what is held — § 411.0745(b) sets the type of fee and not an amount, OCA describes the total as typically about $280 varying by county, call the clerk — and delivers the Rule 145 Statement of Inability as a component rather than as a sentence.
findings.confirmedHere: Yes. The registry's rules.fees records exactly this, including that the $28 belongs to § 411.072(c) and is not a filing fee, and the registry carries a releaseBlocker on the county figure so that no single county number is invented.
findings.doNotRepairThisBy: replacing the OCA range with a single county figure, or deleting the $28 paragraph. This family fails on two other obligations and neither of them is the fee.

contradictingACommittedRecord.what: The MASTER_QUEUE row for ct-decriminalized-set records legalInputStatus SETTLED with legalInputBasis null and laneReturnLegalHold null. The registry entry ct-decriminalized records legalStatus legal_review_pending and carries three entries in buildBlockers, each with impact 'build_blocker': the current scope of 'decriminalized' after State v. Menditto, whether the § 54-142a(k) fee bar reaches § 54-142d, and the accepted filing practice for a § 54-142d petition.
contradictingACommittedRecord.whyNoVerdictHereTurnsOnIt: Under AGENTS.md's build-first review model counsel review is not a blocker through state_built, the registry's releaseBlockers array is empty, and its legalDesignStatus is legal_design_approved_with_limitations. The packet does not depend on any of the three open answers: it refuses to assert decriminalization and carries it as the participant's own position, it states the fee question as unresolved in the registry's own words, and it names the authority for filing practice. The family passes on what it delivers.
contradictingACommittedRecord.forCaptain: The two records disagree in words a reader will act on. Reconciling them is not this lane's to do, but it should not sit unrecorded before any promotion decision on this family.

contradictingACommittedRecord.what: The field map records the instrument for the marijuana route as '...legal_effect_explanation: nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-legal-effect-explanation-3'. contradictingACommittedRecord.what: The report's own note says 'Every written fact value was read back from the extracted text of its component's own pages in the saved packet bytes, not from this builder's intent.' It then records expected "" — an empty string — for all 13 AcroForm writes, with foundInOutputBytes true. A read-back of an empty string against extracted text is satisfied by any document at all.
contradictingACommittedRecord.whyItIsNotScoredAsAFailure: The obligation is about the packet's prefills, and this lane measured them directly: all 13 values are present inside their own widget rectangles in both fixtures. The packet is correct; the evidence file is not load-bearing as written.
contradictingACommittedRecord.forCaptain: Any lane or gate that treats actual-writes.json as proof of a known prefill is, on this family, treating nothing as proof. Worth fixing in the same build script's write-reporting path, and worth checking whether other official_pdf_fill families share the pattern.

ct-decriminalized-set delivers one component more than its committed packet-set manifest declares: the manifest names only ct-decriminalized-primary-filing-1, and the packet also ships ct-decriminalized-filing-instructions-2. rcap-nd-custom-pleading's felony route prints its registry's own stop condition 'Every felony petition, which the controlling review makes an attorney handoff', so the packet ships a felony petition while telling the participant that every felony petition is an attorney handoff. That is the committed record faithfully carried and the honest thing to print, not a contradiction the packet invented.

onThisLanesOwnHistory.whatTheBriefSaid: VF11 as a lane has had verdicts overturned by later re-measurement — one of its Utah failures did not survive a repair, and another lane found its page-18 collision gone at a newer base.
onThisLanesOwnHistory.howThisLaneTreatedThat: As a reason to measure carefully, not as a reason to distrust the lane and not as a reason to soften a verdict. Every one of the five families was scored from zero at this base. The two failures recorded here each rest on something a later reader can re-run in a minute against a named commit: a grep for '411.0735' and a grep for 'other agencies' returning zero on named page ranges, and a word box at named coordinates lying inside a widget rect at named coordinates. If a repair makes any of them false, the verdict should be overturned, and the evidence is written so that overturning it is cheap.

whatThisReturnGrants: Nothing. An independent PASS proves a packet is complete; it approves no output, promotes no family and opens no commercial route. A FAIL is a verdict and a repair assignment, never an edit.
